newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience says had many cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience says had many cooperation talks.

text.p: Biotech specialist Chiroscience Group Plc said on Monday that it had "had talks with many leading pharmaceutical companies" about potential alliances for development of its novel drugs for cancer, asthma and arthritis.
However, in a statement the company gave no further details on the discussions or when an announcement on a keenly-awaited collaboration might be announced.

The company said pre-tax losses in the six months to August 31 widened to 7.3 million stg from 5.5 million a year before, with research and development spending accounting for most of the 45 percent rise in expenditure to 11 million stg.
The Cambridge-based group said Phase 1 clinical trials of its D5410 MMP inhibitor for arthritis showed the drug was "safe and well tolerated".
It said a second Phase 1 study is due to start by the end of 1996, with Phase II trials due to begin in the first half of 1997.

The group's novel anti-asthma project also took a major step forward with the selection of one of its PDE IV inhibitors, D4418, to enter clinical trials during 1997. A cancer compound in the same class as British Biotech Plc's Marimastat could start human trials before the end of 1996.
Chiroscience said its planned marketing application for levobupivacaine, a cleaned up version of an existing local anaesthetic, is on target for late 1997.
The group, which raised 40.3 million stg in a successful placing and open offer at the end of May, said it had cash reserves of 47.7 million stg at the end of August.
